title: `ward run`: status-only HTTPS transport
description: Spec §9.3-9.4. In-process client, HTTPS with verification, no redirects, public-destination-only with DNS results bound to the connection, ambient proxy ignored, bounded timeouts, no automatic retry, status-only output.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T14: the synthetic credential reaches only the mocked approved auth header, never argv, environment, files, output or audit
T15 and T16: redirects are not followed; HTTP, user-info, loopback/private/link-local/metadata, IPv6 variants, DNS rebinding, proxy and TLS-disable attempts are rejected
T17 and T18: credential echoes in any encoding never reach agent-facing output; timeouts and ambiguous mutations report safely without duplicate requests

plan: Re-read spec 9.3-9.4 and ADR 0003 from source; re-measure the private-address rules against the canonical URL form WCLI-9 stores.
Domain: pure destination policy - classify a resolved address as public or not (loopback, private, link-local, multicast, metadata, IPv6 and mapped forms) using maintained parsers.

Adapter: in-process HTTPS client that resolves, validates, then binds the connection to a validated address with hostname verification and SNI retained; no redirects, ambient proxy ignored, bounded timeouts and response bytes, no retry.
Application: `ward run` executes the STORED approved snapshot, never the declaration; status-only result; audit admission before delivery and completion after.
Tests T14-T18 over an injected transport plus a local TLS harness for the binding; credential absent from argv, environment, files, output and audit.
Manifest, docs and security-test matrix; full gate green; independent review; PR.

SLICES DONE. (1) destination policy, src/domain/destination.ts - default-deny over net.BlockList; IPv6 is allow-listed into 2000::/3 and narrowed inside it, IPv4 is judged by the IANA special-purpose registry; IPv4-mapped, NAT64 and 6to4 forms are refused as a class rather than unwrapped, because unwrapping means writing the IPv6 parser spec 9.3 says not to build. (2) the tls.connect adapter, src/adapters/https-transport.ts - one request line, approved headers, credential, Connection: close, then the status line; the body is never read. (3) `ward run` consuming the STORED snapshot, src/application/run.ts + src/application/transport.ts + src/domain/authorization.ts - built from approval.snapshot, never from the declaration, with the declaration only normalized and compared against it first. (4) admission before delivery and completion after, in two separate transactions, so the vault write lock is never held across network I/O; a failing admission blocks the run, a failing completion is reported rather than thrown. (5) audit records in the vault state, with a bounded history. (6) contract wiring: errors, manifest, cli/main.ts, test/contract.test.ts. (7) tests: 24 in test/transport.test.ts against a real socket and a real TLS server, 13 in test/run.test.ts through the command line, 9 in test/destination.test.ts, 2 more in test/project-documents.test.ts.

MEASURED: BUN'S node:https HONOURS AN AMBIENT PROXY, AND tls.connect DOES NOT. This is the whole reason the transport is hand-rolled, so it is recorded with its method. Repro: a net listener on 127.0.0.1, then a request to a host whose `lookup` hook returns a public address. With HTTPS_PROXY set to that listener, node:https connected to the listener while the lookup hook still ran for the destination hostname - so an address-validating hook reported a binding that was not the one used. What failed to defeat it: `proxy: ""`, `proxy: false`, an explicit https.Agent, `agent.createConnection` (never called at all - Bun short-circuits to its fetch layer), and `delete process.env.HTTPS_PROXY` in-process (Bun reads the variables at process start). What does defeat it: NO_PROXY=* set in-process, and - the shape chosen - dialling with tls.connect, which consults nothing but the address it is given. Verified positively: tls.connect to a literal with `servername` set to the hostname reports authorized=true, and Bun refuses an IP passed as servername outright (ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE), so the SNI/IP choice cannot be made silently.

THE FOUR CHECKS OPUM-AGENT ASKED THE REVIEWER TO MAKE ON THE HAND-ROLLED PATH, carried verbatim so the successor does not have to reconstruct them: (1) SNI and hostname verification ACTUALLY ENFORCED - `authorized`, not merely rejectUnauthorized left at its default; (2) no redirect following; (3) the dialled address is the validated one, with no second resolution; (4) a test proving HTTPS_PROXY set in the environment does not change the dial. All four are currently evidenced in test/transport.test.ts, but by this session's own tests, which is not a review. The fourth is the claim-versus-mechanism case and is built with a POSITIVE CONTROL in the same invocation: test/fixtures/transport-proxy-probe.ts runs node:https first (which must reach the parent's listener) and this transport second (which must not), and the assertion is the pair - listener count exactly 1, subject outcome exactly a response. Mutating the subject to use https.request reddens it exactly: the count goes 1 to 2 and the outcome flips - measured, not predicted.

OPUM-AGENT'S 05:32Z RULING, SETTLED THIS SESSION'S WAY. (i) THE WCLI-10/WCLI-11 AUDIT SPLIT: WCLI-10 owns the run path - admission, then delivery, then completion - with the audit as a required injected port whose record type has no field a value could land in, wired to a minimal vault-backed recorder; WCLI-11 keeps `ward audit`, retention and its statement, the fuller field set (observed OS identity, optional self-asserted actor/task labels), and T19. The reasoning, so it is not re-litigated: a `ward run` that delivered without an admission record would violate 9.4, and a no-op port would be the decorative control opum-sdlc forbids. The split is now also written on WCLI-11. (ii) tls.connect plus a status-line-only HTTP/1.1 request is execution and not a design question, because 9.3 requires ignoring ambient proxy configuration and the measurement above shows node:https cannot be made to do that on Bun 1.3.14. (iii) The proxy measurement belongs on this record and on WCLI-19.
